entities.name: CERT-UA
aliases: Computer Emergency Response Team of Ukraine
entities.description: 乌克兰计算机应急响应团队，文档中的披露和告警来源。
entities.evidence_text:
The Computer Emergency Response Team of Ukraine (CERT-UA) has
warned
of a new cyber attack campaign by the Russia-linked APT28 (aka UAC-0001) threat actors using Signal chat messages to deliver two previously undocumented malware families dubbedd BEARDSHELL and COVENANT.

entities.name: PowerShell
entities.description: BEARDSHELL 可下载并执行的脚本环境。
entities.evidence_text: BEARDSHELL, per CERT-UA, is written in C++ and offers the ability to download and execute PowerShell scripts, as well as upload the results of the execution back to a remote server over the Icedrive API.

entities.name: Icedrive API
entities.description: BEARDSHELL 用于回传执行结果的远程服务接口。

entities.name: cross-site scripting (XSS)
entities.description: APT28 利用的跨站脚本漏洞类型。
entities.evidence_text: APT28's exploitation of cross-site scripting (XSS) vulnerabilities in various webmail software such as Roundcube, Horde, MDaemon, and Zimbra to breach Ukrainian government entities.

entities.name: Ukraine
entities.description: 文档中多次出现的攻击目标国家。
entities.evidence_text:
The disclosure comes as CERT-UA
revealed
APT28's targeting of outdated Roundcube webmail instances in Ukraine to deliver exploits for CVE-2020-35730, CVE-2021-44026, and CVE-2020-12641 via phishing emails that ostensibly contain text about news events but weaponize these flaws to execute arbitrary JavaScript.
